beats.narration_text: Salaam. This is Liam, in for Bear. Claude Code has an effort dial, and it's tempting to always turn it up. The better question is how to match effort to the job.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Effort: how much compute Claude spends on a task. An edge case: an unusual input where code tends to break. And slash effort: the Claude Code command that changes the level mid-conversation.

beats.narration_text: So what is effort, really? Thariq Shihipar, in his post Spending your effort, says it gives the model an approximation of how much compute you want it to spend on the task.

beats.narration_text: Think of it like a deadline. Given one hour, you'd bring the best version that meets the task, then expect to iterate. Given twelve hours straight, you'd assume they want you to try very hard.

beats.narration_text: Effort works the same way. Claude always tries to do your task reasonably, but higher effort means more independent action on verification and judgement.

shot.visual_intent: The dial returns at the left, pointer on low, with two short grey columns on the right ('verification', 'judgement'); as the pointer steps up through each level, both columns grow a slab at a time.

beats.narration_text: The clearest case is HTML JS filter, a Terminal-Bench three point oh task: an HTML sanitizer that strips every way of smuggling JavaScript into a page. In Anthropic's runs, Fable five point one on low passed one of five tries: about two minutes, one pass, one hand-written test page.

beats.narration_text: His rule of thumb. Low for quick responses while you're in the loop: brainstorming, sketching, easy changes. Medium for most regular engineering work, like new features.

shot.visual_intent: The big dial on the left; the pointer turns to low and the marker dot jumps beside 'low'; a sketch page draws its doodle ('sketches'); the pointer turns to medium and a feature crate is assembled ('new features').

beats.narration_text: High where verification matters or there are edge cases, like fixing a bug. Max when you want Claude working fully on its own on difficult problems.

shot.visual_intent: The pointer turns to high; a bug appears under a magnifier ring ('bug fixes'); the pointer turns to max and a crate with its own light runs laps on a loop belt, alone ('on its own').

beats.narration_text: And his loop for feature work. Have Claude interview you about the spec. Build it on low. Review it, iterating on low. Then verify and test on high. In Claude Code, slash effort switches the level mid-conversation.

shot.visual_intent: The dial shrinks to the centre; four pills arrive around it (interview, build on low, review, verify on high) joined by ink arrows; a terracotta dot moves to each step as it is spoken while the pointer sits on low, then turns to high at verify; a '/effort' chip drops in and a cursor clicks it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code: Plan one real task with me through the effort loop: name your task. First, interview me about any details I'm missing. Then list which steps to run on low effort and which on high. For the high-effort verification, say exactly what it must check: which edge cases, which tests, and what counts as a failure. Don't build anything yet. Then check two things yourself. Does every high step name something concrete to verify? And build on low, then switch to high with slash effort to verify. Did it catch what low missed?
